sentence: This project tests whether a one-session computer program with text message support helps people handle distress and lowers cannabis use problems.
This project studies how coronavirus RNA and proteins interact as the virus copies and packages its genome.
This project looks for markers that show why triple negative breast cancer responds or resists when radiation is combined with immunotherapy.
This project builds an AI tool that screens facial features to find people at risk of thoracic aortic disease and looks for genetic causes.
This project studies how immune problems in the ileum lead to pouchitis, using patient-derived organoid models to look for predictive markers.
This project processes and combines multi-omics and neuroimaging data to help find blood signs of Alzheimer’s disease over time.
This project builds a mobile health tool that helps public health workers track human and animal health in remote rural areas to investigate zoonotic spillover.
This project offers advanced cellular microscopy and image analysis to help researchers study cells and tissues in rheumatic diseases.
This project studies preterm infants with intraventricular hemorrhage to find early signs that predict who later develops epilepsy.
This project studies how microRNA-146a shapes the foreign body response to biomaterials, including inflammation and fibrosis.
This project builds a blood test based on cell-free DNA to find cancer earlier in peripheral nerve sheath tumors of people with neurofibromatosis type 1.
This project runs high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry of RNA to understand extracellular RNA in colorectal cancer.
This project tries to find out why lipid nanoparticles that carry RNA cause inflammation and then engineers versions that do not.
This project builds a computer model using large language models to turn survey data into predictions of substance use risk.
This project builds a computer model, personalized with left atrial scar patterns, to predict ablation points that stop atrial flutter.
This project studies how a gene mutation shapes the immune response to epigenetic therapy in lung cancer tumor cells.
This project studies how the gut microbiome and bacterial drug metabolism change drug response, using human samples.
This project tests whether early immune cells in the fetal thymus come from a dedicated precursor cell, using fate mapping and perturbation studies.
This project studies how genetic differences linked to addiction affect circadian gene regulation, using mice and machine learning models.
This project tests a urine test that sequences DNA to detect leftover bladder cancer after chemotherapy.
